title: Mount a press's light curtain at its ISO 13855 safety distance
instruction: Stand the light curtain's two posts in the opening in front of the press, one against each side guard, with their lens faces (the broad faces) facing each other across the opening. The beam runs through the posts' centres: put it at the minimum safety distance from the yellow die line's near edge, S = 2000 mm/s x T + 8 x (d - 14 mm), with stopping time T = 0.06 s and resolution d = 20 mm, or up to 20 mm farther.
context: Machine-guarding installers and robot-cell integrators mount safety light curtains in front of presses, press brakes and robot cells at the minimum distance set by ISO 13855: S = K x T + C, with K = 2000 mm/s (while S is at most 500 mm), T the overall stopping time of the machine plus the curtain, and C = 8 x (d - 14) mm for a curtain of resolution d up to 40 mm. Closer than S, a hand that breaks the beam still reaches the die before the press stops. The emitter and receiver posts must also stand against the side guards, so nobody reaches around them, and face each other squarely, or the receiver does not see the emitter. Working out S from the machine's measured stopping time and the curtain's resolution, then setting the posts with a tape from the hazard, is the installer's routine arithmetic and layout.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything except the two posts is fixed to the table. (1) Press: a bench-scale mock, a grey-green painted wooden block 80 mm (x) by 300 mm (y), 140 mm tall, spanning x 44.6-52.6 cm and y -15.0 to +15.0 cm. (2) Opening floor: a light grey rigid PVC plate 246 mm (x) by 280 mm (y), 2 mm thick, spanning x 20.0-44.6 cm and y -14.0 to +14.0 cm, in front of the press. (3) Die line: yellow vinyl tape 6 mm wide, 280 mm long and 1 mm thick, on the floor plate along the press's front, spanning x 44.0-44.6 cm; it marks the die's edge (the hazard), and distances are measured from its near edge, at x 44.0 cm. (4) Side guards: two dark grey steel panels, 246 mm long (x), 10 mm thick and 100 mm tall, running from x 20.0 cm to the press, their inner faces at y +14.0 cm and -14.0 cm (outer faces at +-15.0 cm): the opening between them is 280 mm wide, and their front ends are at x 20.0 cm. (5) Staging mats: two blue rubber mats, 80 x 80 x 3 mm, centred at x 16.0 cm, y +22.0 cm and y -22.0 cm, outside the guards and in front of their ends. (6) Light-curtain posts, loose: the emitter and the receiver, each a black anodised-aluminium box 36 mm deep, 56 mm wide and 100 mm tall, 0.15 kg (a hollow housing with its optics). The lens window is a broad (56 x 100 mm) face; each post's two broad faces are alike (a real build may mark both with red tape as lens windows) and either counts as its lens. Each stands upright on a mat, centred on it, its broad faces toward +x and -x (toward the press and toward the arms): the emitter on the left mat, the receiver on the right. The two posts are identical, so either may go to either guard. Nothing else is on the table. With S = 168 mm (see scoring), the beam belongs 16.8-18.8 cm in front of the die line, x 25.2-27.2 cm; a turned post (36 mm across) against a guard has its centre about 12 cm from the midline.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the two posts' poses (in a real trial: a tape from the die line, a feeler gauge and a top photo). The minimum safety distance is S = 2000 mm/s x 0.06 s + 8 x (20 - 14) mm = 120 + 48 = 168 mm. For each post: 'D' is how far its centre line (the beam passes through the posts' centres) is in front of the die line's near edge, along x; 'gap' is the distance from its outer face (its farthest point toward the nearer guard) to that guard's inner face; 'upright' means its 100 mm axis is within 5 degrees of vertical (either end down); 'on the floor' means its centre is over the floor plate and its lowest point within 3 mm of the plate's top; 'at rest' means its centre, the centre of its top and the centre of a broad face have each moved no more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. A post is 'placed' against a guard if it is upright, on the floor and at rest, its gap is at most 10 mm (touching counts: no gap to reach around it) and 168 <= D <= 188 mm. A placed post 'faces' the other when its lens axis (the line through its two broad faces) is within 5 degrees, seen from above, of the line between the two posts' centres, so the beam meets the lenses squarely. Score 0 if either post's centre, seen from above, is between the guards (up to their outer faces) and less than 168 mm in front of the die line, or past it, at any height, standing or not: a hand breaking the beam there would reach the die before the press stops. Otherwise: 0.25 for each guard with a post placed against it (each guard counts once, so two posts at one guard earn 0.25); if both guards have a placed post, 0.25 more for each of the two that faces the other. Possible scores: 0, 0.25 (one post placed), 0.5 (both placed, neither facing, e.g. not turned), 0.75 (both placed, one facing), 1.0 (both placed, both facing; the trial ends as a success once this has held for 2.5 s, and the score is read from the end state either way). A post farther than 188 mm, more than 10 mm from its guard, tilted, lying down, still on its mat, on top of something or still moving earns nothing for itself and leaves the other post's credit as it is. Facing is judged against the line between the two posts, so posts at different distances face when turned toward each other; squared to their guards 5 mm away, posts at the window's opposite ends (168 and 188 mm) are 4.9 degrees off that line and still face. The scorer sees only the posts, not the grippers: a post held still in place is scored where it stands.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The press, guards, floor plate and tape are fixed boxes. The curtain has no optics, power or controller: the beam is the line through the posts' centres and the lens either broad face of a plain box. The posts stand by gravity (real ones bolt to the floor or the guards). A 60 ms stopping time keeps S on a bench-scale table; real presses give larger S from the same formula. The scorer reads only the posts, not the grippers.
reset_notes: Put each post back upright on its blue mat, centred, broad faces toward the press and the arms: the emitter on the left mat (x 16.0 cm, y +22.0 cm), the receiver on the right mat (x 16.0 cm, y -22.0 cm). Nothing is consumed.
